newsitem.title: USA: P&G stock hit due to Q1 Latam, Asia volume.
newsitem.headline: P&G stock hit due to Q1 Latam, Asia volume.

text.p: Declines in Procter & Gamble Co's first quarter Latin American and Asian volumes drove its stock down Thursday despite record first-quarter earnings that beat Wall Street estimates. It was off 2-3/8 to 93-7/8 mid-afternoon after falling as low as 91-1/2 in the morning.
Analysts said problems are likely short-term in nature and long-term prospects remain strong.
The consumer products giant, which makes Tide detergent and Crest toothpaste, earned $1.39 a share in the first quarter versus $1.27 a year ago. Analysts had expected $1.37.

"Worldwide volume was up one percent. The real shortfall was in Latin America and Asia," Amy Low of Goldman Sachs said. "The good news is margins were well above expectations. That's why earnings came in a couple pennies higher than expected."
Low said P&G will remain on her recommended list and she does not plan to change her $4.75 earnings estimate for the year ending June 30, 1997. It earned $4.29 last year.
"I am (optimistic) about the company's ability to generate 12 percent earnings-per-share growth over time," she said.
William Steele of Dean Witter Reynolds also blamed Latin American and Asian volumes for the stock hit.
But, he said, "I think that the near-term volume weakness will be short-lived."

Steele said, "Earnings were better than anybody forecast. They beat the high end of the range. Sales were pretty much in line (with expectations), and gross margins were stronger than I was forecasting," aided by good cost controls.

"The company is doing what they have to do from a long-term perspective," he said. "(P&G is) leveraging their inherent strengths, which are strong products, great brand promotion and a lean cost structure."

Steele said he thinks P&G's "efficient consumer response," a program to improve efficiencies in promoting and delivering products to retailers, will work in Europe and probably in Asia as well as it has in the United States. It was rolled out overseas later than in the U.S.
"The performance of Procter & Gamble's products is unparalleled," he said. "If they can bring their price down, the (international) consumer will respond positively."

Wesley Roberts of JJB Hilliard, LW Lyons said, "Some volumes in foreign markets were off more than (analysts) expected, but it's something that should iron itself out over the next few quarters. For the long term, it's nothing to be alarmed about, in my opinion."
